title: sUSDe cooldown has two entry points because a share-denominated exit only learns its asset amount after the fact
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.10.5 and A...10.6 expose the same economic action twice: `cooldownAssetsSUSDe(usdeAmount)` names the USDe you want out, `cooldownSharesSUSDe(susdeAmount)` names the sUSDe shares you want to burn.

Both debit the **same** rate-limit key, `LIMIT_SUSDE_COOLDOWN`, and both debit it in **USDe assets** — never in shares. For the assets variant that is trivial and the limit is decreased before the call (A...10.5.2). For the shares variant A...10.6.3 spells out the constraint: "Because the resulting `cooldownAmount` of USDe is only known after the cooldown is initiated, the rate limit ... is decreased at the end of the function using the resulting `cooldownAmount`."

The forcing function is the shared key. Two entry points charging one limit must agree on the unit, or the limit means different things depending on which door was used — and because sUSDe accrues value, a share is a drifting quantity while USDe is a stable one. Denominating in the asset is what keeps the budget interpretable over time.

This is why `cooldownShares` bothers to `abi.decode` its result at all: the return value is not needed for the operation, only for the accounting.
description: cooldownAssetsSUSDe charges LIMIT_SUSDE_COOLDOWN up front from the requested USDe; cooldownSharesSUSDe must decode the returned cooldownAmount and charge the same key afterwards.
